corpusSummary: Across 2026 papers, the corpus reveals a cautious, multi-domain examination of large language models as tools, partners, and drivers of social change. Studies document methodological use (agentic LLMs, policy research, and AI-assisted analytics), mixed-user experiences (trust, adoption, and social capital), and persistent gaps in embodied, situated knowledge, safety, and equity. Together they urge critical governance, human-centered design, and rigorous evaluation in health, education, and policy contexts.

themes.name: AI-augmented research methods and agentic systems
themes.description: A broad set of papers shows LLMs and agentic systems reshaping social science methods, including policy analysis, multi-agent simulations, and workflow tooling, while stressing validation, transparency, and ethical safeguards.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Research across health, education, and everyday contexts examines trust, adoption pressures, social networks, and behavioral responses to AI, revealing both persuasive potential and concerns about dependency and embodiment.

themes.name: Safety, equity, and governance of AI deployment
themes.description: A recurring emphasis on equitable design, safety/readability, literacy, and governance frameworks addresses risks of misinformation, bias, and cultural insensitivity in AI-enabled digital health and education.

themes.name: AI in education and learning design
themes.description: Studies explore AI tutors, scaffolding, literacy, and assessment, highlighting benefits for engagement and personalized learning alongside concerns about overreliance, fairness, and teacher roles.
